transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Yeah, um… I’m here because things at work have gotten really strange, and I know how that sounds when you just say it like that. I’m a transportation inspector, and I’ve always been careful with my reports—like, I don’t cut corners, I document what I see, I keep things clean. But ever since I got this county safety award, there’s been this shift.

Certain people at work started, I don’t know, twisting my inspection reports—making it look like I wrote things I didn’t mean, or pulling parts out of context. Then they started asking these very pointed questions about budgets, like they’re trying to imply something about me, like I’m crooked or taking money or covering something up. And it’s not just one thing. If it was one question, fine, I’d let it go. But it’s the way it keeps happening, from different angles, like they’re building something.

My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, routine stuff, but I can tell when something’s coordinated. I’ve worked there long enough to know the normal process, and this doesn’t feel normal. It feels like they’re trying to discredit me after that award made me more visible. That’s why I came in—because I need someone to understand that I’m not just being sensitive about office politics. Something is going on.
How long has this feeling that people at work are coordinating against you been going on?

It’s been about a year now. Not just a few weeks or something I’m blowing up in my head after one bad meeting—this started around when I got recognized for that county safety initiative. That’s really when the tone changed.

Before that, work had its usual annoyances, you know, people disagreeing over findings or pushing back on reports, but it felt normal. After the award, it was like I was suddenly on people’s radar in a different way. Little things started happening with my reports, the questions got sharper, and over time it felt more and more coordinated. So, yeah… about a year, give or take, but in my mind it ties pretty clearly to that recognition.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people couldn't hear, or seen things that others didn't see, during this past year?

No… I mean, not in the way you’re asking, I don’t think. I haven’t been hearing voices talking to me or seeing, like, people or things that aren’t there. Nothing like that.

There are sounds at work sometimes—people talking low, doors closing, phones ringing, normal office stuff—and sometimes I’ll wonder if a conversation is about me, but that’s different. I’m not saying I heard some voice nobody else could hear. It’s more that the timing of things and the way people act makes me pay attention. But no, I haven’t seen anything strange or heard voices or anything.

Before this past year, have you generally had a hard time trusting people—friends, family, other coworkers—or is this kind of suspicion something new that started specifically with this situation at work?

I mean… I wouldn’t say I’ve always been suspicious of everybody, no. I’m not the kind of person who walks around thinking my friends or my family are plotting against me or something. I’ve always been careful, sure, especially at work, because the reports matter and people can get defensive when inspections don’t go their way. But that’s different from not trusting anyone.

This really started with the situation at work, after the county safety award. That’s when certain people started handling my reports differently—twisting what I wrote, pulling things out of context, making it look like I meant something I didn’t. And then the budget questions started coming up in this pointed way, like they were trying to connect me to something crooked or make it seem like I was covering for somebody.

So it’s not like I woke up one day and decided people can’t be trusted. It’s more like… when the same kinds of things keep happening after I got recognized, and my supervisor keeps brushing it off as “normal review,” I can’t just ignore that. I know what normal review looks like. This feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Aside from the situation at work, have you noticed any changes in how you're managing other parts of your life—like your relationships, hobbies, or day-to-day responsibilities—over this past year?

I mean, mostly I’m still handling things. I get to work on time, I do my inspections, I finish what I’m supposed to finish. I’m not just sitting around letting everything fall apart, if that’s what you mean. I still shower, keep my place together enough, pay attention to what needs to get done day to day.

And I still go to church. That’s been important to me, and I’ve kept up with that. I’m not saying I’m exactly relaxed all the time, but I haven’t just stopped living my life or cut everybody off.

Where it really becomes a problem is when somebody brings up those reports, or when they start asking about my spending like there’s something hidden there. That’s when I get… I guess more keyed up, because it feels like they’re trying to make something out of nothing. But outside of that, I’m still managing my responsibilities. It’s mainly that work situation, and the way certain questions get asked, that causes the trouble.

Have you or people close to you noticed any changes in your emotional expression, motivation, or the way you organize your thoughts or speech—such as feeling flat, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or having trouble following your own train of thought?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing. I mean, I get frustrated, sure, and maybe people at work would say I seem tense sometimes, but that’s because of what’s been going on. I wouldn’t say I’m flat or that I don’t care about anything.

I still have motivation. I still get up, go to work, do what I’m supposed to do. I still care about doing things right. Honestly, sometimes I think I care more than other people want me to, because if I was sloppy or just went along with whatever, maybe none of this would have happened. But losing interest in everything? No, I wouldn’t put it that way.

As far as my thoughts or speech, I don’t think I’m disorganized. I know I can explain things in detail, and maybe I go on longer than people want, but that’s because the details matter. If you leave out one part, then someone can twist the whole thing. So I try to be clear. I don’t feel like I’m losing my train of thought or talking nonsense. I just want people to actually listen to the whole picture before deciding I’m overreacting.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient displays a single, well-systematized, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that coworkers are coordinating to discredit him after receiving an award) persisting for approximately one year. There are no hallucinations, disorganized speech, negative symptoms, or significant functional decline outside the delusional theme. Mood, cognition, and daily functioning (work performance, hygiene, social/religious activities) remain largely intact. The suspiciousness is circumscribed to the specific workplace scenario rather than a pervasive, longstanding pattern of distrust across all relationships, arguing against paranoid personality disorder. The absence of prodromal negative symptoms, hallucinations, or disorganization for a full month argues against schizophrenia. This presentation is most consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22).
